findings.claim: The text-comparison fix covers only the ENVIRON read. In reviewed-each, `split(want, ids, "\n")` yields strnum elements, and these are used as array subscripts (`wanted[ids[i]]`, `hit[...]`, `ids[i] in hit`) with no `""` forcing. On an awk that converts a numeric-looking strnum subscript through CONVFMT (for example `1.0` or `1e0` becoming `1`), reviewed-each would again treat `1.0` as `1`, so it would disagree with reviewed. B15 passes on gawk, mawk and busybox awk, which keep the original string, and the other listed awks are absent or are gawk. The lint `TestEvidenceStore_ReadsEveryEnvironmentValueAsAString` only checks the ENVIRON read, so it would not catch this. This is a robustness gap on awks not installed here, and I did not show that any real awk reaches it.
